title: CHU de Guadeloupe hit by a cyberattack; crisis cell set up and non-urgent care postponed
date_note: RCI (22 November) says the hospital has been under attack since 21h on Saturday evening, 21 November (local time).
geo_basis: hospital's Pointe-à-Pitre site, named by RCI as one of the three affected sites
summary: RCI reported on 22 November that the CHU de la Guadeloupe has been hit by a cyberattack since Saturday evening, 21 November, and that a crisis cell was set up. Telephone, imaging, non-urgent biology, printers and software are down at its three sites, RCI said. Director Eric Guyader said ANSSI described the attack as serious, that recovery will take more than two or three days and that non-urgent activity is postponed for the week.
plain: The main hospital in Guadeloupe was hit by a cyberattack on Saturday night. Phones, imaging and software are down, and the hospital has put off non-urgent care for the week.
exec: A regional hospital lost phones, imaging and software to a cyberattack and postponed non-urgent care, a reminder to test downtime procedures.
action: As RCI relays, the CHU has postponed non-urgent activity for the week and asks people in Guadeloupe who need care to call the emergency medical line before coming to hospital.

key_findings: Cyberattack since 21h Saturday 21 November; crisis cell set up
Telephone, imaging, non-urgent biology, printers and software out at the Pointe-à-Pitre, Perrin and Palais Royal sites
Director Eric Guyader: ANSSI judges the attack serious; recovery not within 2 or 3 days; non-urgent activity postponed for the week

validation.note: One publisher read: RCI, quoting CHU director Eric Guyader. A web search found no second report yet and no CHU notice. RCI's meeting with ANSSI is 'selon nos informations' and is left out. Severity kept at 2 until a second source or official notice is read.
